questions.q: Why did Rehoboam go to Shechem?
questions.a: Rehoboam went to Shechem because all Israel was coming there to make him king.

questions.q: Who came with the assembly of Israel to speak to Rehoboam?
questions.a: Jeroboam the son of Nebat came with the assembly of Israel to speak to Rehoboam.

questions.q: What did Israel ask of Rehoboam?
questions.a: All Israel asked that Rehoboam would lighten the heavy yoke his father had put on them.

questions.q: For how many days did Rehoboam send the people away?
questions.a: Rehoboam sent the people away for three days.

questions.q: With whom did Rehoboam consult?
questions.a: Rehoboam consulted with the older men who had advised Solomon his father.

questions.q: What did the older men say to Rehoboam?
questions.a: The older men said that Rehoboam should speak kindly to the people of Israel.

questions.q: What did Rehoboam do with the advice the older men gave him?
questions.a: Rehoboam decided not to follow the advice of the older men.

questions.q: What did the younger men tell Rehoboam to say to the people?
questions.a: The younger men told Rehoboam to say, “I am going to rule you much more harshly than my father did.”

questions.q: What did Rehoboam say he would use to punish the people?
questions.a: Rehoboam said he would use scorpions to punish the people.

questions.q: What had the king instructed the people to do?
questions.a: The king had instructed the people to come back on the third day.

questions.q: How did the king answer the people?
questions.a: The king answered the people harshly.

questions.q: What did the king say he would do with the yoke on the people?
questions.a: The king said he would add to the yoke on the people.

questions.q: Who brought about these events?
questions.a: These events were brought about by Yahweh.

questions.q: What did all Israel say when they saw that the king did not listen to them?
questions.a: All Israel said they would go home and not be ruled by Rehoboam. They said he can rule his own tribe but not the others.

questions.q: Over what people did Rehoboam become king?
questions.a: Rehoboam became king over the people of Israel who lived in the cities of Judah.

questions.q: What did Israel do to Adoram?
questions.a: All Israel stoned Adoram to death with stones.

questions.q: Who followed the family of David?
questions.a: Only the tribe of Judah followed the family of David.

questions.q: Why did Rehoboam assemble the house of Judah in Jerusalem?
questions.a: Rehoboam assembled the house of Judah to fight against the house of Israel to return the rest of the kingdom to him.

questions.q: To whom did the word of God come?
questions.a: The word of God came to Shemaiah the man of God.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say?
questions.a: Yahweh said, “You must not attack or fight against your fellow Israelites. Instead, go home.”

questions.q: Where did Jeroboam build Shechem?
questions.a: Jeroboam built Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim.

questions.q: What did Jeroboam think in his heart?
questions.a: Jeroboam thought in his heart, “Now the kingdom will return to the house of David.”

questions.q: What did Jeroboam say about the people offering sacrifices in the temple of Yahweh?
questions.a: Jeroboam said, “If these people offer sacrifices in the temple of Yahweh, they will kill me and return to Rehoboam king of Judah.”

questions.q: What did King Jeroboam make?
questions.a: King Jeroboam made two calves of gold.

questions.q: Where did Jeroboam set up the two calves of gold?
questions.a: King Jeroboam set up one calf in Bethel and one in Dan.

questions.q: What people did Jeroboam make into priests?
questions.a: Jeroboam made priests of the people who were not among the sons of Levi.

questions.q: What did Jeroboam do at Bethel?
questions.a: Jeroboam made a feast at Bethel like the feast that was in Judah.

questions.q: What did Jeroboam do at the altar in Bethel?
questions.a: Jeroboam went up to the altar to burn incense.

commentary.text: Rehoboam's accession, The people's petition, His rough answer.

Verses 1–15 The tribes complained not to Rehoboam of his father's idolatry, and revolt from God. That which was the greatest grievance, was none to them; so careless were they in matters of religion, if they might live at ease, and pay no taxes. Factious spirits will never want something to complain of. And when we see the Scripture account of Solomon's reign; the peace, wealth, and prosperity Israel then enjoyed; we cannot doubt but that their charges were false, or far beyond the truth. Rehoboam answered the people according to the counsel of the young men. Never was man more blinded by pride, and desire of arbitrary power, than which nothing is more fatal. God's counsels were hereby fulfilled. He left Rehoboam to his own folly, and hid from his eyes the things which belonged to his peace, that the kingdom might be rent from him. God serves his own wise and righteous purposes by the imprudences and sins of men. Those that lose the kingdom of heaven, throw it away, as Rehoboam, by wilfulness and folly.

The people speak unbecomingly of David. How soon are good men, and their good services to the public, forgotten ! These considerations should reconcile us to our losses and troubles, that God is the Author of them, and our brethren the instruments: let us not meditate revenge. Rehoboam and his people hearkened to the word of the Lord. When we know God's mind, we must submit, how much soever it crosses our own mind. If we secure the favour of God, not all the universe can hurt us.

Jeroboam distrusted the providence of God; he would contrive ways and means, and sinful ones too, for his own safety. A practical disbelief of God's all-sufficiency is at the bottom of all our departures from him. Though it is probable he meant his worship for Jehovah the God of Israel, it was contrary to the Divine law, and dishonourable to the Divine majesty to be thus represented. The people might be less shocked at worshipping the God of Israel under an image, than if they had at once been asked to worship Baal; but it made way for that idolatry. Blessed Lord, give us grace to reverence thy temple, thine ordinances, thine house of prayer, thy sabbaths, and never more, like Jeroboam, to set up in our hearts any idol of abomination. Be thou to us every thing precious; do thou reign and rule in our hearts, the hope of glory.
